legend: You are given an array a$$$a$$$ of length n$$$n$$$ and an integer m$$$m$$$. Find three distinct indices 1≤i,j,k≤n$$$1 \le i, j, k \le n$$$ such that m≤ai+aj+ak≤2m$$$m \le a_i + a_j + a_k \le 2m$$$, or report that no such indices exist.
input: Each test consists of multiple test cases.
The first line of input contains a single integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤104$$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases.

The first line of each test case contains two integers n$$$n$$$ and m$$$m$$$ (3≤n≤2⋅105$$$3 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$, 1≤m≤3⋅108$$$1 \le m \le 3 \cdot 10^8$$$) — the length of the array a$$$a$$$ and the target sum, respectively.
The second line of each test case contains n$$$n$$$ integers a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ (1≤ai≤108$$$1 \le a_i \le 10^8$$$) — the array a$$$a$$$ as described above.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n$$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed 2⋅105$$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output: For each test case, if there is no solution, print a single integer −1$$$-1$$$.
Otherwise, print three distinct integers i$$$i$$$, j$$$j$$$, k$$$k$$$ (1≤i,j,k≤n$$$1 \le i, j, k \le n$$$) such that m≤ai+aj+ak≤2m$$$m \le a_i + a_j + a_k \le 2m$$$.
If there are multiple solutions, you may print any.
note: In the first test case, we have a2+a3+a4=19$$$a_2 + a_3 + a_4 = 19$$$, which is in the range [10,20]$$$[10, 20]$$$.
In the second test case, it can be shown that no triple satisfies the condition 20≤ai+aj+ak≤40$$$20 \le a_i + a_j + a_k \le 40$$$.
